newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends volatile session barely lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends volatile session barely lower.

text.p: After climbing steadily throughout the session, NYCE cotton futures succumbed to trade selling near the close to settle barely weaker.

The see-saw activity bounced the most-active December contract above and below unchanged. In early dealings, fund buying buoyed the contract over resistance seen at 77.75, the recent high made September 4. Trade selling at the highs pressured December into negative territory late in the day, however.
The contract settled at 77.21, off 0.01, having ranged from 77.90 to 76.60. The back months closed 0.26 to 0.05 firmer.
Volume was estimated at a brisk 18,000 lots.
"From a momentum standpoint, not closing above 77.50 is fairly disappointing," said David Brandon, an analyst with Smith Barney.
"We had a good battle between the funds, who still think it's going higher, and the trade, who see this as a good hedging opportunity," Brandon said.
Market sources attribute bullish sentiment on the market's focus on supply.
While demand remains sluggish, talk of a reduced crop in China, coupled with fears that the U.S. crop could fall to around 17.0 million 480-lb bales, could lend support to prices.
Rain and cold temperatures forecast for North Texas for the remainder of the week, could keep prices higher.
